title: Inspector rejects garden fence appeal on Town House Road, Littleborough
excerpt: A planning inspector has upheld Rochdale Council's decision to refuse retrospective planning permission for a garden fence at 19 Town House Road, Littleborough, citing its negative impact on the area's character.

body:
A planning inspector has ruled against a homeowner's appeal regarding a garden fence at 19 Town House Road, Littleborough. Caterina Buonocore had sought retrospective planning permission for a 1.55-metre high boundary fence, which is approximately twice the height of the original fence. The council had previously rejected her application, leading to the appeal.

In the inspector's decision, it was stated that the main concern was the fence's effect on the character and appearance of the area. The inspector noted that boundary treatments in the locality are typically low-level and visually permeable, contributing to a sense of openness and allowing the greenery in front gardens to be appreciated. The inspector remarked that the existing vegetation helps to soften the street scene, enhancing the area's character.

The inspector further explained that the close-boarded timber fence introduced by the appeal contrasts sharply with the more traditional forms of boundary treatment found in the neighbourhood. Observations made on-site indicated that, due to the prominent corner location, the fence appeared particularly stark and incongruous against the backdrop of traditional stone terraces with lower boundary treatments.

As a result of this ruling, Buonocore may now be required to remove the fence, which could have implications for her property and the surrounding area. The decision underscores the importance of maintaining the character of local neighbourhoods and adhering to planning regulations.
